sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home, U.P. Lko.
Counsel for Applicant :- Shailesh Kumar Pathak,Anju Tripathi,Saurabh Pathak
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
2. In terms of the F.I.R. lodged as a missing person report, it was alleged that the daughter of the informant was enticed away by the applicant.
Subsequently, in the statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C., the victim stated that as she was unhappy with her parents as such she has gone on her own to Lucknow where she met the applicant.
Nothing wrong was stated against the applicant.

However,
in the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., for the first time it was stated that physical relations were made against the consent of the victim.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant argued that in the statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C., the victim did not support the prosecution story.

However, for the first time, in the statement under Vijay Yadav vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home, ... on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186972149/
1 Section 164 Cr.P.C., the victim has stated that the physical relations were formed by the applicant against her consent.

entities.text: Vijay Yadav vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The victim refused to undergo medical examination.
The age of the victim is around 20 years.
The applicant is in jail since 15.11.2022 having no criminal history, hence the applicant may be enlarged on bail.
4. Learned A.G.A. also opposed the prayer for bail.

5. Considering the variance in the two statements of the victim recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. coupled with the fact that the applicant has no criminal antecedents and is in custody since 15.11.2022 and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail,
would in any way adversely affect the trial
and without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
6. Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

7. Let the applicant Vijay Yadav be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No.223 of 2022, under Sections 366, 376 and 506 I.P.C., Police Station Haiderganj, District Ayodhya on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions :-
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
Order Date :- 16.4.2024 Shukla  Vijay Yadav vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home, ... on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186972149/
